key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Can be sudden or gradual. LOCATION: Chest (palpitations). DURATION: Minutes to persistent. CHARACTER: Regular RAPID palpitations, "flutter" sensation. AGGRAVATING: Exertion, stress. RELIEVING: Cardioversion, rate control medications. TIMING: Paroxysmal or persistent. SEVERITY: Discomfort, not severe pain. KEY POSITIVES: Regular rapid heart rate (often 150 bpm with 2:1 block), dyspnea, lightheadedness, sawtooth pattern on ECG, history of AFib or structural heart disease. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT irregularly irregular (AFib), NOT sudden start/stop (SVT typically).
